text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.4% today as oil prices surged on escalating geopolitical risk in the Middle East. Iran intensified attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, driving U.S. crude sharply higher to around $102 per barrel—a move that directly boosts the earnings outlook for oil producers like ConocoPhillips. The company benefits immediately when the price it sells oil for rises, and the 15.6% gain over two weeks reflects the cumulative effect of this regional tension pushing crude higher.

The underlying supply concern is real: tanker rates have spiked significantly as shipping becomes riskier, adding roughly $38 per barrel to the effective cost of moving physical oil globally. For an oil producer, this kind of geopolitical friction—combined with signals that the U.S. won't escalate militarily (which could have caused even more disruption)—creates a environment where crude stays elevated without the risk of a wider conflict that might ultimately constrain demand.
